lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At exactly midnight, your fingertips start to glow. Not a lot. Just enough to light up the paperclip on your desk.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You poke it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It doesn't look like gold. It IS gold. Heavy. Cold. Real.

lines.speaker: NINA
lines.text: …Why is your paperclip shiny?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You look at your hand. The glow is gone. One touch. That's all you get. But tomorrow at midnight, it comes back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So… what if you could turn one thing into gold every single day?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It takes you a week to figure out the rules. Mostly by getting them wrong.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Rule one: it's the first thing you touch after midnight. Not the thing you want. The first thing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Night two, you fall asleep waiting. You wake up hugging a solid gold pillow.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Worst. Nap. Ever.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Rule two: gloves don't help.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: They just turn into very expensive gloves.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Rule three: it's forever. You can't turn anything back. Ever.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So every night at 11:59, you sit very, very still… and you choose.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day three: a spoon. Your mom stirs her coffee with it for a week before she notices.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day four: your old bike.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Here's what nobody tells you about gold. It's heavy — about two and a half times heavier than steel. And it's soft. So soft you can dent it with your teeth. That's why pirates in movies bite their coins.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Gold bike: zero stars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day five, your best friend Theo has an idea.

lines.speaker: THEO
lines.text: Touch my phone. A golden phone. Do it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You touch it.

lines.speaker: THEO
lines.text: …Where's the screen?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Everything turns to gold. The glass, the battery, the chips. Your touch doesn't make a gold phone. It makes a phone-shaped paperweight.

lines.speaker: THEO
lines.text: My mom's gonna kill me.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then you get smart. A shop downtown buys gold by weight. No questions. Well… a few questions.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day eight, the rent is paid. Day ten, the hospital bill from last winter: gone. Day twelve, your mom quits the late shift.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And Nina asks for one thing.

lines.speaker: NINA
lines.text: Can I eat gold?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Technically… yes. Chefs put thin gold leaf on fancy cakes. It's safe. It does absolutely nothing. It goes in… and it comes out.

lines.speaker: NINA
lines.text: Gold poop.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Gold poop.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But why is gold worth so much in the first place? Because there's so little of it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Take all the gold humans have ever dug up. Every coin, every ring, every bar in every bank vault. Melt it together, and it makes a cube about twenty-two meters on each side. That's it. All of it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And nobody on Earth knows how to make more. Much of the gold in the universe was forged when two dead stars — neutron stars — smashed into each other. The gold in your mom's ring is older than the Earth.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: For thousands of years, people tried to make it anyway. They called it alchemy. And just once, we did it. Inside the Large Hadron Collider, physicists fired lead atoms past each other for years… and made gold. About 29 trillionths of a gram. It lasted less than a millionth of a second.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That's real.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You make more gold than that before breakfast.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day fourteen, you get greedy. You touch an old car in the junkyard.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A gold car weighs as much as a small truck. And it's worth more than your whole street.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The next week, it's on the news.

lines.speaker: NEWS ANCHOR
lines.text: …mysterious gold flooding local markets…

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And something weird starts happening. The price of gold starts to fall.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: This has happened before. In 1324, Mansa Musa, the king of Mali and one of the richest people who ever lived, passed through Cairo on his way to Mecca. Historians say he gave away so much gold that it lost value there for years.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Gold is only worth a lot because there isn't much of it. And now there's you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Theo comes over. He's quiet.

lines.speaker: THEO
lines.text: My grandma saved gold her whole life. Rings, a necklace. For emergencies. The shop says it's worth less now.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He doesn't say it's your fault. He doesn't have to.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Every bit of gold you make makes everyone else's gold worth a little less. Grandmas. Families. Whole countries keep gold in their vaults to protect their money.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day twenty-six. A grey car parks across the street. It doesn't leave.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day twenty-seven, there's a knock.

lines.speaker: SUIT
lines.text: We know what you can do. Here's how this goes. One touch a day — for us. We decide what you touch. We decide where the gold goes. In return, your family never worries about money again.

lines.speaker: MOM
lines.text: And if he says no?

lines.speaker: SUIT
lines.text: Then someone else will find him. Someone less polite.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He leaves the folder on the table. Inside: a photo of your house. And a photo of Nina's school.

lines.speaker: SUIT
lines.text: We'll pick you up on day thirty. Just before midnight.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Day thirty. 11:50 p.m.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Mom is pacing. Theo snuck in through the back door. Nina is supposed to be asleep.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You've thought about everything. Running. Hiding. Saying yes. But every road ends the same way: midnight comes, your fingers glow, and someone else decides what you touch. Forever.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 11:58. Footsteps on the porch.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 11:59. The door opens.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And from the stairs, a little voice.

lines.speaker: NINA
lines.text: Don't go!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She's running at you. Arms wide. Bare hands. The first thing you touch.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two seconds.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Step back, and she hits the floor — and she'll try again. Reach for the suit, and they'll know exactly how dangerous you are. There's only one thing in this room you can touch that ends all of this.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You press your glowing fingertips into your own palm.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nina crashes into you. She's warm. She's laughing. She's not gold.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Your hand is. And your fingertips are gold too. They can't glow anymore. The touch is gone. For good.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The man in the suit looks at your hand. Then at his folder. Then he closes it.

lines.speaker: SUIT
lines.text: …Well. That's that.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He walks out. The grey cars leave, one by one.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The next morning, your right hand is solid gold. It's heavy. You're learning to write with your left.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nina doesn't care. She holds your gold hand all the way to school like it's the coolest thing in the world.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Maybe it is.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You turned thirty things into gold. Only one of them was worth it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So what would YOU touch first? Tell us in the comments.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And if you want to know who's next… subscribe for part two.
